# Requirements Quality Checklist: Gestión de trabajos y horas becarias

**Purpose**: Unit tests for the clarity, completeness, consistency, and measurability of the frontend requirements.
**Created**: 2026-10-30
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are the responsibilities and permitted actions of Becario, Encargado, and Administrador explicitly distinguished? [Completeness, Spec §User Scenarios & Testing]
- [x] CHK002 Are requirements defined for discovery, application, acceptance/rejection, closure, attendance, hour accreditation, evaluation, and administrative supervision? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001–FR-020]
- [x] CHK003 Are the frontend requirements explicitly tied to the completed backend contract revision `openapi.yaml` v1.4.0? [Dependency, Plan §Technical Context]
- [x] CHK004 Are requirements defined for both the primary data states and the absence of data, including no jobs, no applications, no history, and no rating? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK005 Are the conditions for creating an evaluation unambiguous: closed job, accepted application, confirmed attendance, and owning Encargado? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014–FR-015]
- [x] CHK006 Are the four evaluation criteria and their allowed values explicitly defined as Responsabilidad, Puntualidad, Proactividad, and Comunicación from 1 to 5? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014]
- [x] CHK007 Is the phrase “últimos 10 trabajos realizados” defined using closure, confirmed attendance, ordering, and deterministic tie-breaking rules? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017–FR-019]
- [x] CHK008 Is the behavior for fewer than 10 realized jobs explicit, including the null rating and exact message `faltan realizar trabajos`? [Clarity, Spec §FR-019]
- [x] CHK009 Are “horas realizadas”, “faltantes”, and “excedentes” defined using the backend minute fields rather than ambiguous decimal-hour calculations? [Clarity, Spec §Key Entities; Plan §Technical Context]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK010 Are the web requirements consistent with the backend contract’s response envelope, pagination metadata, error shape, CSRF requirement, and idempotency rules? [Consistency, Contract §Reglas obligatorias del cliente]
- [x] CHK011 Do the requirements consistently state that evaluations never alter attendance, accredited minutes, progress, or administrative compliance? [Consistency, Spec §FR-020; Spec §Success Criteria]
- [x] CHK012 Are the requirements consistent about evaluation immutability, with no implied edit or delete flow elsewhere in the specification? [Consistency, Spec §FR-016; Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK013 Are the scope statements consistent about evaluations being included in this delivery rather than optional or deferred? [Conflict, Spec §Clarifications; Spec §Assumptions]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK014 Can each user story be accepted independently using the stated user journey, actor, preconditions, action, and outcome? [Acceptance Criteria Quality, Spec §User Scenarios & Testing]
- [x] CHK015 Are the success criteria objectively measurable for task completion time, authorization, accessibility, response time, rating calculation, and no-hour-change behavior? [Measurability, Spec §Success Criteria]
- [x] CHK016 Are the expected outcomes for valid evaluation creation and each relevant failure category (`400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `409`) described sufficiently for a reviewer to distinguish them? [Completeness, Contract §Calificaciones disponibles]
- [x] CHK017 Is the criterion for a successful administrative view explicit about which hour fields are shown and which evaluation fields must be excluded? [Clarity, Spec §US3; Spec §FR-020]

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK018 Are primary scenarios documented for each role, including the Becario rating journey and the Encargado evaluation journey? [Coverage, Spec §User Stories 1–3]
- [x] CHK019 Are alternate scenarios defined for rejected applications, absent participants, excess hours, missing evaluations, and fewer than 10 realized jobs? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK020 Are exception scenarios defined for unauthorized roles, inactive accounts, non-owner Encargados, duplicate applications, and duplicate evaluations? [Exception Flow, Spec §Edge Cases; Spec §FR-011–FR-016]
- [x] CHK021 Are recovery or retry requirements defined for failed asynchronous reads and failed evaluation submission without implying duplicate evaluations? [Gap, Recovery Flow]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK022 Are concurrent acceptance and cup-limit conflicts described as a user-visible requirement rather than only an implementation concern? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK023 Is the behavior for a repeated evaluation submission explicitly distinguished from a retry of the same request and from a new duplicate evaluation? [Ambiguity, Contract §Contract rules]
- [x] CHK024 Are requirements defined for partially missing or incomplete API data, including missing pagination metadata or missing optional evaluation data? [Gap, Exception Flow]
- [x] CHK025 Are timezone and date-boundary expectations specified for work start, work end, closure eligibility, and display? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK026 Are accessibility requirements specific enough to cover keyboard operation, labels, focus behavior, validation summaries, and responsive presentation for every interactive evaluation and management flow? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013; Spec §SC-005]
- [x] CHK027 Are performance targets defined for the critical job, progress, rating, and administrative journeys without relying on framework-specific implementation terms? [Coverage, Spec §SC-006]
- [x] CHK028 Are privacy requirements explicit about which student information an Encargado may see and that Administrators do not receive evaluation scores? [Security, Spec §FR-011; Contract §Authorization matrix]
- [x] CHK029 Are error-message requirements defined in user terms while preserving the canonical backend error categories? [Clarity, Contract §Reglas obligatorias del cliente]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK030 Is the mandatory cross-repository dependency rule stated clearly enough to determine when a web task must stop and backend work must resume? [Dependency, Plan §Cross-Repository Blocking Rule]
- [x] CHK031 Does the specification identify the backend OpenAPI contract as the sole source of truth and explicitly prohibit parallel frontend contracts or unverified mocks? [Dependency, Plan §Technical Context]
- [x] CHK032 Are assumptions about the single UPB institution, single active period, fixed roles, and backend-owned authorization explicitly bounded? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK033 Are the exact contract fields used by the web documented without duplicating or contradicting the canonical backend contract? [Traceability, Contract §Fuente canónica]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK034 Is the meaning of “calificación visible” unambiguous about whether it refers to the aggregate rating, individual evaluation averages, or both? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-017–FR-019]
- [x] CHK035 Is it clear which Encargado-facing screen or context exposes an existing evaluation and how the requirements distinguish “already evaluated” from “eligible to evaluate”? [Gap, Spec §US2]
- [x] CHK036 Are the terms “trabajo realizado”, “trabajo cerrado”, “asistencia confirmada”, and “evaluación disponible” defined consistently across the spec and contract summary? [Terminology, Spec §Key Entities; Contract §Calificaciones disponibles]
- [x] CHK037 Are the boundaries between requirements quality, implementation tasks, and backend contract ownership explicit enough to prevent this checklist from being interpreted as an implementation test? [Consistency, Plan §Notes]

## Notes

- All items are intentionally unchecked and require reviewer judgment.
- Mark items `[x]` only after confirming the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- `/speckit.implement` may read checklist state as a gate but must not modify these markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit.specify` and `/speckit.clarify`.
